comments.author: @LifeinNovaScotiaCanada
comments.text: From the Halifax waterfront down to Peggy's Cove, this documentary captures why living on the East Coast is truly unbeatable! Gorgeous footage of our wild Atlantic shore. Incredible watch!

replies.author: @Earthcue
replies.text: Thank you! ❤️ Peggy’s Cove has such a special coastal charm. Is Nova Scotia home for you, or did you fall in love with it on a visit?

comments.text: strange AI video. Hopewell Rocks is not in Nova Scotia and some of the aerial views are reversed (maybe for copyright reasons) where vehicles are driving on the wrong side of the road. Video editing is also weird, can be talking about Kejimkujik for example and showing aerial views of Lunenburg. Good documentary overall though.

replies.author: @Earthcue
replies.text: Thanks for pointing that out! 🙏 You’re right about Hopewell Rocks. The video isn’t AI generated, though. We research and edit everything ourselves, but we use licensed footage from different sources, so a few clips can sometimes be mislabeled or matched incorrectly. Really appreciate the detailed feedback!

comments.author: @TravelBeyond4K
comments.text: The weather along those Cabot Trail cliffs shifts in minutes from blinding fog to sheer ocean exposure. That relentless Atlantic wind and the massive tide swings at Fundy really show how unforgiving this edge of Canada is. It is wild, raw maritime geography at its absolute purest.

replies.author: @Earthcue
replies.text: That’s what gives Nova Scotia such a powerful character. The weather and tides can make the landscape feel completely different from one moment to the next.
